gap: The supplied code establishes registration, notification, tallying, and the successful completion branch, but omits Raft field declarations and leaderLoop initialization. These dependencies are needed to construct a legal isolated fixture and observe actual completion without copying the completion logic into the harness.
partial_design: Retain O_verify_voter_support and all five selected bindings. Construct fixed membership with local voter L, remote voters V1 and V2, and nonvoter N. Use actual Raft.verifyLeader, followerReplication.notifyAll, and verifyFuture.vote calls. Deliver only N's affirmative contribution in the primary case; independently derive contributor eligibility from configured ServerID and Suffrage. Include a separate permitted case delivering V1's affirmative contribution. Existing methods control registration and synchronous notification delivery; buffered channels can capture terminal notifications without sleeps or transport-order assumptions. A terminal tally notification alone does not establish successful future completion. Inspect leaderLoop setup to determine how to execute its actual result branch and stop independently of verification success. Record registration, contributor delivery, bounded completion, and final result under a stable operation ID. Compare actual successful completion against independently computed voter support. Fixture construction and withheld background workers must be declared adaptations; distributed response reachability and stale reads remain unresolved. No additional producer or filter is proposed.
